About Us
New Rush Hall School (NRHS) is a specialist school for pupils aged 5 to 16 whose primary area of need is social, emotional and/or mental health (SEMH). Based in the London Borough of Redbridge, we welcome pupils from Redbridge and a number of neighbouring local authorities.
NRHS has 80 commissioned places across its primary and secondary phases and is currently operating with approximately 100 pupils on roll. Our pupils are supported by a multi-disciplinary team of around 90 staff, including teachers, pastoral leaders, therapists, mentors, instructors and support staff. This enables us to provide highly personalised academic, pastoral and therapeutic support while maintaining high expectations for every pupil.
Inclusion is at the heart of everything we do. We recognise that many of our pupils have experienced significant barriers to education, but we do not believe these should define their future. Our broad and ambitious curriculum provides pupils with a wide range of learning opportunities, progressing to meaningful GCSE and vocational qualifications that prepare them for further education, training and employment.
We are equally proud of the opportunity’s pupils experience beyond the classroom. Personal development is central to life at NRHS, with an extensive programme of enrichment, cultural experiences, residentials and more than 150 educational visits each year. These experiences help pupils discover new interests, develop confidence and independence, build positive relationships and understand the wider world.
Strong relationships underpin everything we do. Our staff work together to understand each pupil as an individual, helping them to overcome barriers, develop emotional regulation, engage successfully with learning and recognise their own potential. We want pupils to leave NRHS not only with meaningful qualifications, but with positive experiences of education, greater confidence in themselves and genuine aspirations for their future.
At NRHS, personalisation never means lowering expectations. It means finding the right route for every pupil to succeed.

pageCache.pageTitle: Ethos, Vision & Values - New Rush Hall School
pageCache.text:
Ethos, Vision & Values
At New Rush Hall School (NRHS) our Ethos has clear vision and values.
Ethos
Where doors are opened, resilience built and attitudes and lives are transformed.
Vision
Learning and developing together for achievement.
Our aim is that all members of our school community learn together to achieve. We want all pupils at NRHS to have opportunities in the wider world and to help remove barriers that they may face. We work endlessly to encourage pupils to be resilient and to continue to succeed and work hard even when it seems things are not going as planned. We want our pupils to be confident with positive attitudes and perseverance so they can be successful in their own way and enjoy the journey along the way.
Values
Friendship, respect, equality, courage, determination, perseverance, resilience and inspiration.
Friendship Positive relationships are fundamental to life at NRHS. Our small classes and nurturing environment give pupils opportunities to develop their social skills, build trust and form positive relationships with their peers. Through learning, enrichment, trips, residentials and shared experiences, pupils learn what it means to be a good friend and to develop relationships based on trust, kindness and mutual support.
Respect We expect everyone within our school community to treat others with respect. Staff model this through positive relationships and unconditional positive regard, while pupils are supported to develop empathy and understand the impact that their words and actions can have on others. We celebrate difference and teach pupils to engage respectfully with people whose backgrounds, beliefs, experiences or views may be different from their own.
Equality Inclusion and equality are at the heart of NRHS. We teach pupils to understand both equality and equity: treating people fairly does not always mean treating everyone in exactly the same way. We recognise individual need and remove barriers wherever we can, while ensuring that all pupils have access to ambitious learning, meaningful experiences and opportunities to succeed.
Courage Courage can mean trying something new, asking for help, speaking up when something is wrong or continuing when something feels difficult. We create a school environment in which pupils feel safe to take positive risks, express themselves and stand up for themselves and others. We encourage pupils to challenge discrimination, inequality and unkindness rather than being a bystander.
Determination We want pupils to develop the belief that setbacks do not have to determine what happens next. At NRHS, pupils are encouraged to set ambitious goals, keep striving when things are difficult and find another way forward when something does not work first time. Through learning, careers education and the wider opportunities available to them, we help pupils recognise what is possible and develop the determination to pursue it.
Perseverance Every day provides another opportunity to make progress. We teach pupils that meaningful achievement and personal development take time and that progress is not always straightforward. Through personalised targets, recognition and encouragement, pupils learn to keep going, reflect on their progress and understand that improvement comes through sustained effort over time.
Resilience We want pupils to develop the confidence to face challenges and recover when things do not go as planned. Our classrooms provide safe environments in which making mistakes is recognised as part of learning. Pupils are encouraged to reflect, learn from experience, try again and develop strategies that will help them manage challenges both in school and beyond it.
Inspiration We want pupils to be inspired by what they learn, the people they meet and the opportunities they experience. Staff share their own enthusiasm and expertise, while our curriculum, enrichment programme, careers events, visitors, trips and experiences expose pupils to new ideas and possibilities. We also celebrate the achievements and destinations of former NRHS pupils, showing our current pupils where their own ambitions might take them.

pageCache.pageTitle: Therapeutic Support - New Rush Hall School
pageCache.text:
Therapeutic Support
Therapeutic support is an integral part of life at New Rush Hall School (NRHS) and a defining feature of our specialist SEMH provision.
We recognise that pupils are best able to engage with education when they feel safe, understood and emotionally ready to learn. Our therapeutic approach therefore sits alongside and within our academic provision, helping pupils to overcome barriers, develop emotional regulation, build confidence and resilience, strengthen relationships and successfully engage with learning.
Our approach is personalised and responsive. We know that one size does not fit all and that pupils’ needs can change over time. Every pupil benefits from a strong universal therapeutic offer, with additional targeted or specialist interventions provided where these are needed.
Our Universal Therapeutic Offer
Therapeutic practice is embedded throughout the school day and begins with the relationships pupils develop with the adults around them. All pupils benefit from:
A Graduated Approach
Where a pupil needs support that is additional to our universal offer, we provide a broad range of therapeutic interventions matched to individual need.
Our current therapeutic pathways include:
Mentoring – Trusted one-to-one relationships that support pupils to develop self-awareness, confidence, emotional regulation, positive behaviour and strategies for overcoming barriers to learning.
Counselling – Individual therapeutic support providing pupils with a safe and supportive space to explore difficulties, understand their emotions and develop healthier coping strategies.
Therapeutic Support for Children Looked After – Targeted support for children looked after and previously looked after pupils, recognising the particular impact that experiences of loss, separation and disrupted attachment can have.
Boxing – Structured physical activity used to develop discipline, resilience, confidence, self-regulation and positive approaches to challenge.
Personal Training – Individualised fitness programmes that promote physical wellbeing, confidence, self-esteem, motivation and goal-setting.
Lego Therapy – Structured sessions supporting communication, teamwork, shared attention, problem-solving and positive social interaction.
Sensory Support – Access to calm, low-stimulus environments and appropriate sensory strategies to support regulation and reduce anxiety.
Music – Creative opportunities, including music production, that enable pupils to develop confidence, self-expression, emotional awareness and new skills.
Horticulture – Practical, nature-based activities that promote wellbeing, patience, responsibility and resilience.
Cooking – Therapeutic and practical experiences that develop confidence, independence, communication and wider life skills.
Alongside these interventions, targeted PSHE and other personalised programmes may be used to respond to particular vulnerabilities or areas of need.
The Right Support at the Right Time
Therapeutic support at NRHS is flexible. Some pupils may benefit from a short-term intervention at a particular point in their school journey, while others require more sustained support. Provision may be delivered individually, in small groups or through creative, practical and physical approaches depending on what is most appropriate for the pupil.
Our therapeutic, pastoral and teaching teams work closely together so that support does not operate in isolation. Pupils’ progress and changing needs are regularly reviewed using staff observations, pupil voice, attendance and engagement information, behaviour patterns, EHCP outcomes and, where appropriate, information from families and other professionals.
As pupils develop new skills and greater independence, support can be adapted, reduced or changed. The aim is not for pupils to remain dependent upon therapeutic intervention, but for them to develop strategies, confidence and resilience that they can increasingly use for themselves.
We evaluate therapeutic support by considering the difference it makes to pupils’ everyday lives. This includes improvements in emotional regulation, confidence and self-esteem, relationships, attendance, engagement with lessons and pupils’ ability to manage challenges successfully.
Most importantly, we listen to our pupils. Their experiences and views help us understand what is working, shape individual provision and continually develop our therapeutic offer.
At NRHS, therapeutic support and education are not separate. They work together to help pupils feel safe, overcome barriers, engage with learning, recognise their strengths and achieve their potential.

pageCache.pageTitle: Reading at NRHS - New Rush Hall School
pageCache.text:
Reading at NRHS
At New Rush Hall School (NRHS), we recognise reading as a cornerstone of academic success, social mobility and lifelong learning. As a specialist SEMH provision, we understand that secure literacy skills are essential if pupils are to access the wider curriculum, demonstrate their academic potential and successfully prepare for life beyond school.
Our ambition is for every pupil to leave NRHS as a confident and increasingly fluent reader who can engage meaningfully with a wide range of texts, achieve success in their qualifications and develop a genuine enjoyment of reading. We see reading not simply as a skill to be mastered, but as a gateway to independence, confidence, cultural awareness and future opportunity.
Many pupils join NRHS having experienced barriers to reading or with gaps in their literacy knowledge. Some may lack confidence or associate reading with previous difficulties in education. We identify pupils’ individual starting points carefully and provide the support, challenge and encouragement they need to make progress.
Our approach has two equally important aims: to ensure that pupils develop the reading skills they need to succeed academically, and to create a culture in which reading is valued, accessible and enjoyable.
Pupils learn to read so that they can read to learn.
Reading is at the heart of our Primary curriculum and forms part of pupils’ learning every day.
Pupils develop their reading through a structured combination of phonics, targeted intervention, a daily Reading Carousel, story time, teacher-led reading, classroom book corners and regular opportunities to use the school library. Trained staff provide additional support with decoding, fluency and confidence according to individual need.
Our Reading Carousel provides regular opportunities for pupils to develop decoding, fluency and comprehension, while teachers read aloud each day to model fluent and expressive reading and expose pupils to a broad range of vocabulary and texts.
Pupils requiring additional support with early reading receive structured phonics teaching and targeted intervention. As their skills develop, pupils progress from decodable texts towards increasingly challenging books matched to their reading development and interests.
Alongside learning the mechanics of reading, we want Primary pupils to experience the imagination, curiosity and enjoyment that books can provide and begin to see themselves as readers.
Reading in Secondary
As pupils progress into Secondary, the emphasis increasingly moves from learning to read towards using reading confidently and independently to learn.
Reading is developed not only through English but across the curriculum. Teachers have access to pupils’ reading information and use this to inform the texts they select, the questions they ask and the scaffolding, intervention and challenge they provide. This helps ensure that literacy difficulties do not become unnecessary barriers to accessing subjects across the curriculum.
Structured form-time reading, regular access to the school library and opportunities for guided, peer and independent reading help pupils develop fluency, confidence, comprehension and reading stamina.
As pupils move towards Key Stage 4, reading is increasingly connected to their qualifications and preparation for examinations. Support focuses on areas such as functional literacy, vocabulary, fluency, comprehension of examination texts and, where appropriate, individual examination access needs.
Assessment and Targeted Support
Reading provision at NRHS is driven by a detailed understanding of each pupil rather than assumptions based on their age or year group.
We use Star Reader and Accelerated Reader as important elements of our whole-school approach to assessment and reading development. Star Reader provides standardised reading-age information which helps staff identify strengths and areas for development, set appropriate expectations and monitor progress. Pupils are assessed at three points during the academic year so that progress can be reviewed and intervention adapted where necessary.
Accelerated Reader supports pupils to select books within their appropriate Zone of Proximal Development (ZPD), providing texts that offer suitable challenge without creating unnecessary frustration. Comprehension quizzes, feedback and individual goals help pupils develop independence and take greater ownership of their reading.
Pupils requiring further support may access our Additional Learning Support (ALS) programme. Intervention is informed by baseline and standardised assessment and can address areas including phonics, decoding, fluency, comprehension and wider literacy development.
Where older pupils have gaps in foundational reading skills, we use age-appropriate intervention and resources, including Little Wandle Rapid Catch-Up and Talisman materials where appropriate. This enables pupils to address gaps in phonics and decoding without accessing materials that feel inappropriate for their age.
Our approach is equally ambitious for pupils who are already confident readers. Higher-level readers are encouraged to engage with increasingly complex literature, extended non-fiction, ambitious vocabulary and opportunities that develop deeper comprehension, inference, analysis and critical thinking.
Reading Across the Curriculum
Reading is everyone’s responsibility at NRHS.
Teachers and support staff understand the importance of literacy in enabling pupils to access their subjects. Reading information is shared with staff and used to inform curriculum planning, classroom adaptation, questioning, scaffolding and appropriate challenge.
Our support staff also play an important role in developing reading. They provide individual and small-group intervention, scaffold reading within lessons and help pupils develop the confidence to read aloud and attempt challenging texts.
Importantly, we recognise the relationship between pupils’ literacy development and their wider social and emotional needs. Reading information can form part of our Pupil Passport discussions, helping staff understand literacy barriers alongside each pupil’s wider SEMH needs and ensuring approaches remain consistent across school.
Reading for Pleasure and Enrichment
Developing technically competent readers is only part of our ambition. We want pupils to discover books and texts that interest, challenge and inspire them.
Our school library is central to developing this culture. The collection is continually developed to provide engaging and age-appropriate texts that reflect a wide range of identities, backgrounds and experiences. We want pupils both to see themselves reflected in the literature they encounter and to experience perspectives that broaden their understanding of others and the wider world.
Reading also forms part of our wider enrichment and cultural capital programme. World Book Week involves pupils from Year 1 through to Year 11 and has included author visits, creative writing workshops, book fairs, competitions, themed activities and opportunities for pupils to respond creatively to literature.
Through these experiences, we aim to show pupils that reading extends far beyond the classroom and can provide enjoyment, inspiration, knowledge and opportunities to understand both themselves and the world around them.
The impact we seek goes beyond improvements in reading ages. We want pupils to become increasingly confident, independent and resilient readers who can use literacy successfully across the curriculum and in their everyday lives.
As pupils’ decoding, fluency, vocabulary and comprehension improve, they are increasingly able to access challenging curriculum content, engage successfully with qualifications and develop the literacy skills required for further education, employment and adulthood.
We also recognise the emotional impact that becoming a more confident reader can have. Pupil voice tells us that pupils increasingly describe reading as enjoyable, feel proud of the progress they make and experience greater confidence when reading aloud or approaching unfamiliar texts. Secondary pupils have also described reading as becoming less stressful and more personal as their confidence develops.
Ultimately, our ambition is for pupils to leave NRHS understanding that reading is something they can do, something that can open doors for them and, importantly, something they can enjoy.

Enrichment
At New Rush Hall School (NRHS), our Enrichment Curriculum provides pupils with opportunities to learn and develop beyond traditional academic subjects. Enrichment forms an important part of our wider curriculum and provides structured opportunities for pupils to explore interests, develop new skills and experience success in different areas of school life.
The programme is designed particularly with the social, emotional and personal development of our pupils in mind. Through a broad range of practical, creative, physical and interest-based activities, pupils have opportunities to develop confidence, communication, independence, teamwork and positive relationships with both peers and adults.
Enrichment also provides pupils with opportunities to discover strengths and interests that may not always emerge within traditional classroom learning. Trying something new, persevering when an activity is challenging and experiencing success can help pupils develop a more positive view of themselves as learners and build the confidence to approach new experiences.
All activities within our Enrichment Curriculum are carefully considered and support our school values of courage, determination, equality, friendship, inspiration, perseverance, resilience and respect.
Our enrichment offer is reviewed each year and adapted to reflect the needs and interests of our pupils. Activities also provide opportunities to support individual EHCP outcomes and wider personal development priorities, ensuring that enrichment is purposeful as well as enjoyable.
The Enrichment Curriculum looks different across our Primary and Secondary phases, reflecting pupils’ age, stage of development and individual needs.

Careers Information and Guidance
At New Rush Hall School (NRHS), we are committed to ensuring that every pupil develops the knowledge, skills, confidence and aspirations they need for life beyond school. Our Careers Education, Information, Advice and Guidance (CEIAG) programme is an important part of this, preparing pupils for further education, training and employment.
Careers education begins in the primary phase, where pupils are introduced to different jobs, careers and aspirations through age-appropriate learning and experiences. As pupils progress through the school, the programme becomes increasingly personalised, with careers guidance, employer encounters, workplace and vocational experiences, visits to colleges and training providers, and opportunities to explore a broad range of post-16 pathways.
At NRHS, we believe that high-quality careers education can be a powerful driver of social mobility. It raises aspirations, broadens horizons and challenges the limitations that pupils may place on themselves or that others may have placed upon them. Through meaningful experiences, strong partnerships and personalised support, we aim to empower every pupil to recognise their strengths, make informed choices and approach their future with confidence and ambition.
Throughout Year 1 – 5 pupils will have the opportunity to:
Throughout Year 6, 7, 8 and 9, all pupils will have had the opportunity to:
Throughout Year 10 – 11 all pupils will have had the opportunity to:
Career Guidance Meetings Pupils are entitled to appropriate guidance to meet their individual needs. All pupils at school can request an appointment with the Careers Lead, although Year 10 & 11 will have scheduled termly appointments. Pupils are identified for careers meetings based on need and through self-referral.
Career information Career information is delivered through a range of curriculum areas, it is also available to pupils within the Key Stage 4 Hub, through relevant displays and through assemblies. This information includes a range of career guides, apprenticeship and employer information, as well as guides on job-search activities.
External providers Ranges of external providers are invited into school to support the careers programme. These might include local colleges, universities, training providers, apprenticeship organisations, employers, school alumni, or staff from various projects.
Employer links Links with employers, businesses and other external agencies continue to grow by building on local community connections with a view to offer pupils experience in the world of work.
Careers Education in the Curriculum PSHE is offered to all pupils across the school; there is explicit careers guidance and units of work designed to support all pupils in their destinations. Careers, information and guidance will also permeate throughout the wider school curriculum enabling pupils to link their learning to a range of potential future career pathways.
Gatsby Benchmark The Gatsby Benchmark is a framework which is used by the school to assess the development of our pupils’ employability skills.
Our Careers Team are guided by the 8 benchmarks to provide our pupils with the best careers education, information, advice and guidance.

pageCache.pageTitle: Headteacher's Message - New Rush Hall School
pageCache.text:
A Message From Our Headteacher
Welcome to New Rush Hall School (NRHS). I am incredibly proud to lead a school that believes passionately in what every young person can achieve.
Many of our pupils come to NRHS having experienced significant challenges in their lives or previous education. It is important that we understand those experiences and the impact they may have had, but equally important that they do not define what happens next. Our pupils deserve the same ambition, opportunities and expectations as any other young person.
That belief shapes everything we do.
We provide the specialist support our pupils need alongside an education that challenges them, creates opportunities and prepares them for life beyond NRHS. At the heart of this is a committed staff team who build strong relationships with pupils and families and who genuinely want every young person to succeed.
We want pupils to achieve meaningful qualifications, but education is about much more than what appears on a certificate. It is about discovering interests and talents, experiencing new things, building positive relationships, developing confidence and independence, and beginning to see possibilities for the future.
Inclusion sits at the heart of our school. We know that every pupil is different and that what works for one may not work for another. We will adapt, find different ways to engage and keep trying when things don’t work first time, but we will never use a pupil’s needs or previous experiences as a reason to expect less of them.
Above all, I want every pupil to leave NRHS knowing that they were understood, challenged and believed in; proud of what they have achieved and confident that their past does not determine their future.
NRHS is a place where doors are opened, resilience is built and attitudes and lives are transformed.
Mr Sam Walters Executive Headteacher

P.E. and Sports Premium
At NRHS all Primary pupils access P.E. lessons over the course of the week. In addition to this, they have scheduled swimming, horse-riding and cycling lessons throughout the school year. In Secondary, P.E. and sporting activities form part of the scheduled curriculum and extra-curricular activities.
Physical activity has numerous benefits for children and young people’s physical health, as well as their mental wellbeing (increasing self-esteem and emotional wellbeing and lowering anxiety and depression) and can also have wider benefits for pupils, improving behaviour, encourages teamwork and strengthens peer relationships as well as enhancing academic achievement.

pageCache.pageTitle: It's GCSE Results Day - New Rush Hall School
pageCache.text:
It’s GCSE Results Day
There was plenty to celebrate at New Rush Hall School (NRHS) on GCSE Results Day, as our Year 11 pupils returned to school to collect a fantastic set of results.
We are incredibly proud of what this group of young people has achieved. There were some excellent individual results across a range of subjects, with many pupils achieving or exceeding their target grades. For many of our pupils, their journey through education has not always been straightforward, making their achievements even more special.
Results Day was full of smiles, celebrations and some very proud pupils and staff. Most importantly, all of our leavers have secured a post-16 destination and are now ready to take the next step in their education, training and future careers.
A huge congratulations to all of our pupils and a massive thank you to the staff who have supported them along the way, often going the extra mile to help them achieve their very best.
We will certainly miss this group of young people at NRHS, but we are incredibly proud of them and look forward to hearing about their successes in the future.
Congratulations, Class of 2026!

pageCache.pageTitle: Pastoral Leads - New Rush Hall School
pageCache.text:
Pastoral Leads
At New Rush Hall School (NRHS), we know that pupils are best able to engage with learning when they feel safe, understood and supported. Our Pastoral Leads play an important role in creating this environment and ensuring that pupils receive the right support at the right time.
Pastoral Leads work closely with pupils throughout the school day, building strong and trusting relationships and developing a detailed understanding of each young person. They support pupils with attendance, engagement, emotional regulation, relationships and behaviour, helping them to overcome barriers and successfully access learning.
They also provide an important link between home and school. Pastoral Leads work closely with parents and carers, teachers, therapists, mentors and other professionals to ensure that support is joined up and responsive to each pupil’s needs. Where concerns arise, we aim to communicate with families early and work together to address them before they become more significant.
In our Primary phase, pastoral support is structured differently to reflect the way the phase operates. Primary pupils spend the majority of their school day with their class teacher and a consistent class team, meaning relationships, communication and pastoral support are embedded throughout the day. Class teachers are therefore central to identifying and responding to emerging needs and maintaining regular communication with families. This is overseen and supported by the Associate Assistant Headteacher who holds pastoral responsibility across the Primary phase.
In our Secondary phase, each year group has a designated Pastoral Lead, providing pupils and families with a consistent point of contact and ensuring that pastoral support is coordinated as pupils progress through the school.
Our pastoral approach reflects our school values of friendship, respect, equality, courage, determination, perseverance, resilience and inspiration. Alongside providing support when things are difficult, our pastoral teams celebrate success, recognise progress and help pupils develop the confidence, independence and skills they need both in school and beyond.

Safeguarding
Safeguarding is everyone’s responsibility and is at the heart of everything we do at New Rush Hall School. The safety, welfare and wellbeing of our pupils is our highest priority, and we are committed to providing an environment in which every young person feels safe, heard, valued and supported.
We recognise that effective safeguarding is about more than responding when a concern arises. It is about knowing our pupils well, building trusted relationships, identifying concerns early and working together with families and other professionals to provide the right support.
All staff receive regular safeguarding and child protection training and understand their responsibility to recognise, report and respond to concerns. We maintain robust safer recruitment procedures and ensure that the appropriate statutory checks are completed for adults working within our school.
Safeguarding is also embedded throughout our curriculum and wider personal development programme. Pupils are taught how to recognise and manage risk, build healthy relationships, seek help when they need it and keep themselves and others safe. This includes learning about online safety and the risks pupils may encounter both within and beyond school.
We want pupils to feel confident that there is always an adult at NRHS they can speak to if they are worried about themselves or someone else, and that when they speak, they will be listened to and taken seriously.
Any concerns regarding the safety or wellbeing of a pupil should be raised with a member of the Safeguarding Team.

Curriculum
At New Rush Hall School (NRHS), we provide a broad, ambitious and personalised curriculum designed to meet the needs of our pupils while maintaining high expectations for what they can achieve.
Our curriculum aims to empower pupils with the knowledge, skills, qualifications and resilience they need to overcome barriers, pursue their aspirations and successfully prepare for life beyond school. Academic learning sits alongside an extensive programme of personal development, enrichment, careers education and vocational opportunities, ensuring that pupils are prepared not only for their next stage of education or training, but for adulthood and the wider world.
We recognise that pupils arrive at NRHS with different experiences, starting points and needs. Our curriculum is therefore carefully adapted to enable pupils to engage and succeed without limiting ambition. From Primary through to Year 11, learning is designed to build progressively, address gaps in knowledge and provide meaningful pathways towards recognised qualifications and future destinations.
In Years 1 to 6, pupils study a broad curriculum designed to develop strong foundations in literacy and numeracy alongside knowledge and understanding across a wide range of subjects.
Mathematics and the Reading Carousel take place daily. The Reading Carousel provides targeted activities according to pupils’ individual needs and includes reading, writing, phonics and comprehension.
English, Science, History, Geography, PSHE and RE are taught through themed learning, with topics developed over a weekly or fortnightly period. Pupils also study Art, Design & Technology, Computing, Spanish, PE and Horticulture.
In Years 7 to 9, pupils follow a broad curriculum comprising English, Mathematics, Science, Construction, Spanish, History, Geography, Food Technology, Performing Arts, Computing, Music, Art, PE and PSHE.
During the Summer Term of Year 9, pupils begin to consider and select their Key Stage 4 options. Our qualification offer is reviewed regularly to reflect pupils’ needs, interests and future aspirations and provides opportunities to pursue both academic and vocational pathways.
Options may include subjects such as Art, History, Food Technology, Business Studies, Geography, Music and Construction.
In Years 10 and 11, all pupils continue to study the core curriculum of English, Mathematics and Science alongside PE, Performing Arts and PSHE.
Pupils also continue with the option subjects selected during Year 9, working towards a personalised programme of recognised academic and vocational qualifications. This combination enables pupils to develop their individual strengths and interests while preparing for appropriate post-16 pathways.
Our curriculum extends far beyond the classroom. Pupils across all year groups have access to a comprehensive enrichment programme designed to broaden experiences, develop interests and talents, promote our school values and support pupils’ social, emotional and personal development.
Through enrichment, educational visits and wider experiences, we aim to give pupils opportunities to experience places, activities and possibilities that they may not otherwise encounter and to develop the confidence and cultural capital needed for life beyond NRHS.
Work Experience, Employability and Preparation for Adulthood
Preparing pupils successfully for their next steps is an important part of our curriculum.
Pupils have opportunities to develop employability skills through our Employability and Preparing for Work programme. This includes a six-week Employability course alongside opportunities to explore external work experience and develop workplace skills through internal placements.
These experiences help pupils develop independence, communication, teamwork and an understanding of the expectations of the workplace, while enabling them to explore potential careers and make informed decisions about their future.

Cultural Capital
At New Rush Hall School (NRHS), we believe that education should open doors to experiences, places and opportunities beyond the classroom. Developing pupils’ cultural capital is therefore an important part of our curriculum and wider personal development offer.
For many of our pupils, previous experiences of education, social disadvantage or individual circumstances may have limited their opportunities to explore the wider world. We are determined that these barriers should not limit their future. Our Cultural Capital programme provides all pupils with opportunities to broaden their horizons, raise aspirations and develop confidence, independence and a sense of belonging.
Bringing Learning to Life
Across each academic year, pupils take part in over 150 planned trips, visits, events and experiences. These include curriculum-linked educational visits, museums and galleries, theatres, places of worship, careers experiences, guest speakers, themed events, recreational activities and residential opportunities.
These experiences are carefully planned to complement learning in the classroom. Whether visiting a cultural venue linked to a subject, experiencing a workplace or college, travelling somewhere unfamiliar or taking part in a residential, pupils have opportunities to apply their learning, experience something new and develop important social and practical skills.
Building Confidence and Independence
Our Cultural Capital programme is carefully sequenced from Primary through to Year 11. Younger pupils begin with shorter and more familiar experiences before progressing towards increasingly ambitious visits, longer journeys, complex public environments and residential experiences.
For our pupils, the experience itself can be just as important as the destination. Travelling independently, managing an unfamiliar environment, interacting with new people, trying something for the first time or staying away from home can represent significant achievements and help develop resilience, confidence and independence.
Importantly, our Cultural Capital trips and experiences are provided free of charge to pupils. We want opportunity to be determined by what will benefit a pupil, not by their family’s ability to pay.
Ultimately, Cultural Capital at NRHS is about broadening pupils’ understanding of the world, developing their confidence to participate in it and helping them recognise the opportunities available to them beyond school.

Year 10
Staff across each subject area have worked hard to develop a curriculum that meets the needs of our pupils.
Please click on the links below to get more information as to what pupils will be studying across each curriculum each 1/2 term:
Subject intent
The information below highlights the intent behind each subject in Year 10, including the knowledge and skills we aspire for pupils to achieve.
English
At NRHS, the Key Stage 4 English curriculum intends to foster the pupils’ interest in Literature and Language. In the realm of Language, our goal is to nurture confident speakers who can adeptly present ideas in a formal context, actively listen to feedback, and pose questions to clarify information—all while using standard English. In the field of Literature, our intention is to expose pupils to a diverse range of texts and genres from the literary canon, ultimately transforming them into inquisitive yet critical readers. In the context of writing, our aim is to cultivate effective writers who can skilfully deploy figurative language and analyse texts. These skills are pivotal for obtaining a recognised qualification and gaining entry to a chosen career pathway.
Maths
At NRHS, the Key Stage 4 maths curriculum intends to embed key mathematical skills so that pupils can become fluent in the fundamentals of mathematics, reason mathematically, and problem solve by applying their skills and knowledge. We intend to consolidate pupils’ understanding of mathematical concepts and develop their mathematical competency and fluency. This will in turn enable pupils to apply their mathematical knowledge and skills to gain recognised qualifications, which will give them access to post-16 courses and the world of work.
Science
At NRHS, the Key Stage 4 science curriculum aims to cultivate curiosity and foster an inquisitive mindset about the universe. Our lessons revolve around the development of scientific inquiry skills, including classifying, comparing and contrasting, predicting, making models, gathering data, measuring, and finally, observing. The intention is to expand upon and deepen pupils’ scientific knowledge while enhancing their understanding of ideas and concepts introduced in earlier Key Stages. Given that the subject is taught across the disciplines of Biology, Chemistry, and Physics, our goal is to broaden and nurture pupils’ interests in specific areas of science, with the ultimate aim of obtaining a GCSE qualification, or equivalent. The study of science at Key Stage 4 provides pupils with a foundation for more advanced studies, laying the groundwork for a diverse range of careers.
Art
At NRHS, the Key Stage 4 art curriculum aims to enhance pupils’ resilience and creativity through focused independent exploration of materials, processes, thoughts and their own ideas. It is intended that pupils will have the freedom to express themselves imaginatively and inventively. Pupils will develop skills to contextualise and critically analyse historical and contemporary artforms, ensuring a meaningful and valuable artistic experience within their journey. It is intended that pupils will be able to understand the many different progression pathways available to them within the arts and gain a valuable insight into how art is embedded throughout much of today’s culture and society.
Business Studies
At NRHS, the Key Stage 4 business studies curriculum intends for pupils to take a journey through the world of business, providing them with the knowledge and analytical skills required to make business decisions and become Entrepreneurs of the future. It is intended that pupils will foster a growth mindset, discover a deep-rooted passion to innovate, and recognise the qualities required to succeed in business, in the fast-paced, global business environment in which we live; all whilst gaining a GCSE qualification.
Construction
At NRHS, the Key Stage 4 construction curriculum intends to prioritise practical, job-focused activities, thoroughly preparing pupils for the working world. Through hands-on experiences, it is intended that pupils acquire essential skills in various construction areas, promoting personal development and maturity. This curriculum not only enhances technical proficiency but also cultivates planning and organisational skills crucial for life after school. Connecting classroom learning to real-world applications, it equips pupils with practical knowledge and vocational skills vital for success in the construction industry. The ultimate aim is to ensure a smooth transition into the professional world or Further Education, where pupils are well-prepared and confident in their abilities.
Food Technology
At NRHS, the Key Stage 4 food technology curriculum intends for pupils to explore the art of cooking and food innovation. Focused on practical application, the curriculum supports pupils in developing vital skills linked to the nutritional value of food, as well as discovering different cooking techniques. The curriculum intends to provide pupils with practical and theoretical learning opportunities so that they have skills and knowledge required to access an appropriate qualification pathway whether it be at BTEC L2 or a GCSE qualification.
Geography
At NRHS, the Key Stage 4 geography curriculum intends to develop pupils’ understanding of the physical and human processes that shape our world. Pupils will investigate contemporary geographical issues through a range of places, environments and case studies, developing their ability to interpret maps, data and geographical evidence. Through fieldwork and geographical enquiry, pupils will collect, present, analyse and evaluate information. The curriculum encourages pupils to consider different perspectives, assess sustainability and make informed, evidence-based judgements about real-world issues. Pupils will develop their geographical knowledge, critical thinking and examination skills, preparing them for further study and life beyond school.
History
At NRHS, the Key Stage 4 history curriculum intends to refine pupils’ historical understanding, critical analysis and independent research skills. Pupils are encouraged to explore connections, causation and differing perspectives. Through engaging with primary and secondary sources, the curriculum intends to cultivate a nuanced appreciation for historical contexts. Additionally, the curriculum aims to prepare pupils for further academic pursuits and instil a sense of historical curiosity. This will empower pupils to navigate the complexities of the modern world with a well-informed historical perspective, allowing them to achieve a recognised qualification.
Music
At NRHS, the Key Stage 4 music curriculum intends to not only focus on helping pupils to express themselves creatively through performance and composition but also includes preparing pupils for music industry careers. This comprehensive program ensures pupils not only cultivate a thorough understanding of music but also acquire practical skills, providing them with the essential knowledge for successful endeavours in the dynamic music industry. The curriculum aims to empower pupils with a well-rounded musical education that prepares them for a variety of opportunities and challenges; all whilst gaining a BTEC qualification.
PE
At NRHS, the PE curriculum intends to adhere to the philosophy of ‘Sport for All’. The school aims to deliver an exciting and enjoyable experience for all pupils acquiring the skills and knowledge in line with the National Curriculum. The broad and balanced curriculum aims to re-cap, re-call and build on prior knowledge using a range of physical activities. Through a carefully structured programme, we aim for pupils to build their physical, social and mental skills, enabling them to fully participate in a range of roles in PE. All pupils at NRHS have the opportunity to participate in an extensive Extra Curricular/Enrichment programme, which develops pupils’ confidence in applying their skills in competitive situations.
Performing Arts
At NRHS, the Key Stage 4 performing arts curriculum intends to develop confident, creative and increasingly independent performers and media practitioners. Pupils will build on their performance and production skills through practical projects involving drama, digital media and visual storytelling. They will develop their ability to plan, rehearse, create, perform, film, edit and evaluate work for different audiences and purposes. Through collaboration, reflection and feedback, pupils will refine their creative and technical choices while developing communication, resilience and teamwork. The curriculum provides opportunities for pupils to explore increasingly complex themes and prepares them for the vocational expectations of performing arts.
PSHE / RSE
At NRHS, the Key Stage 4 PSHE curriculum intends to build on knowledge, skills and attributes for navigating future pathways into a healthy, safe and successful adulthood. Pupils explore their attitudes, values and beliefs, developing understanding of others perspectives. The curriculum focuses on the use of distanced and experiential learning opportunities so pupils can practice managing influence and risk, learning to make informed decisions about health, relationships, financial capability, future learning and employability. As part of the PHSE curriculum, pupils are taught RE to foster an understanding and respect of different faiths and diversity within the community. The curriculum intends to ensure our pupils are prepared for life in the modern world, equipped to live as happy, healthy and fulfilled adults, able to navigate diverse and ever-changing communities and work-places. Parents have the statutory right to withdraw their child from the sex education element of the RSE curriculum.
Sports Science
At NRHS, the Key Stage 4 BTEC sports science curriculum intends to develop pupils’ knowledge, practical skills and understanding of sport and physical activity. Pupils will explore sports equipment and technology, preparation for exercise, components of fitness, rules, officiating and methods of improving performance. Through practical activities, research and vocational scenarios, pupils will apply their knowledge to different sports and participants. The curriculum aims to develop leadership, communication, teamwork and decision-making while encouraging pupils to analyse performance and identify opportunities for improvement. Pupils will develop the knowledge and confidence required to successfully complete vocational assessments and progress through the BTEC sports science qualification.

Subject intent
The information below highlights the intent behind each subject in Years 1 & 2, including the knowledge and skills we aspire for pupils to achieve.

Our structured synthetic phonics programme, intends to support pupils to develop confidence and the skills needed to read and write cohesively. By creating an immersive experience, we cultivate pupils’ natural curiosity, inspiring them to become lifelong learners with a positive attitude towards reading and writing. Through developing their English skills pupils will go on to be confident when sharing and expressing themselves.
Maths
At NRHS, the Key Stage 1 Maths curriculum intends to embed key mathematical skills so that pupils can become fluent in the fundamentals of mathematics, reason mathematically, and problem solve by applying their skills and knowledge. We intend to build on pupils’ natural curiosity about the world by exploring mathematical concepts through play and creative experiences helping them to make connections between maths and everyday life. This in turn helps them to develop confidence and mental fluency with whole numbers, counting and place value. We aim to develop pupils’ mathematical vocabulary when solving problems.
Science
At NRHS, the Key Stage 1 Science curriculum intends to encourage pupils to be inquisitive and to foster their curiosity about the universe by asking and answering questions. Learning is based around scientific enquiry skills: classifying, comparing and contrasting, predicting, gathering data, measuring, observing. We intend for our pupils to be equipped with the scientific skills required to understand the uses and implications of science, today and for the future.
Art
At NRHS, the Key Stage 1 Art curriculum intends to give pupils opportunities to express themselves whilst exploring a range of media and art in the environment. The Art curriculum engages and inspires pupils to invent and create their own works of art, through exploration of different artists. Pupils will develop their critical thinking and evaluation skills. Through exposure to different artists and techniques, pupils will develop and extend creative and expressive elements and be provided with opportunities for them to express their individual thoughts, interests and ideas. Moreover, it enables pupils to develop a natural sense of wonder and curiosity about the world around them.
Computing
At NRHS, the Key Stage 1 Computing curriculum intends to inform and inspire pupils living in a digital world. Pupils will understand the importance of using technology in their daily lives for work and leisure. We aim to ensure pupils can use technology safely and are exposed to a range of devices found in the modern world. Through developing their understanding of online safety and allowing them to access devices and programs, we intend to support them in an ever-changing digital society.
Design & Technology (DT)
At NRHS, the Key Stage 1 DT curriculum intends is to explore pupils’ creativity and imagination so that they can express themselves in a variety of ways. Reflection and critical thinking skills are developed through the research, refine, create and evaluate model as part of class projects. The aim of this is to develop pupils’ problem-solving skills, trial and error processes, to improve their work and take pride in it. The curriculum also intends to improve pupils’ life skills are enhanced by the opportunity to explore practical experiences using equipment safely.
Geography
At NRHS, the Key Stage 1 Geography curriculum intends to create a lifelong love of the subject by encouraging pupils to become curious about the UK with a specific focus on our local community. Pupils will go on a journey learning about their community, diverse places within their community, local history, and local people. The curriculum aims for pupils to develop a connection and love for their community and the UK as a whole. The curriculum intends to foster a deep connection to the UK gaining knowledge about the human and natural environments, encouraging pupils to ask questions and develop their enquiry skills so that pupils can ask questions about the world.
History
At NRHS, the Key Stage 1 History curriculum intends to foster in the pupils a sense of curiosity about their own history, as well as that of the local area. The curriculum will enable them to develop an understanding of important figures and events. It is intended that the pupils will think critically and discuss evidence as they develop a sense of wonder and interest about both past and present and start to understand their place in the chronology of the world in which they live
Horticulture
At NRHS, the Key Stage 1 Horticulture curriculum intends for pupils to go on an adventure into the natural world. The curriculum will introduce pupils to the basic skills and knowledge in the production of food crops. The curriculum intends to provide pupils with the opportunity to nurture their wellbeing in a safe, outdoor space so that they can develop their confidence, patience and perseverance. The curriculum will enable pupils to explore the relationships between living things and the environment, whilst promoting independent thinking and learning.
PE
At NRHS, the PE curriculum intends to adhere to the philosophy of ‘Sport for All’. The school aims to deliver an exciting and enjoyable experience for all pupils acquiring the skills and knowledge in line with the National Curriculum. The broad and balanced curriculum aims to re-cap, re-call and build on prior knowledge using a range of physical activities. Through a carefully structured programme, we aim for pupils to build their physical, social and mental skills, enabling them to fully participate in a range of roles in PE. All pupils at NRHS have the opportunity to participate in an extensive Extra Curricular/Enrichment programme, which develops pupils’ confidence in applying their skills in competitive situations.
PSHE
At NRHS, the Key Stage 1 PSHE curriculum intends to promote self-awareness of pupils’ personal development and social interactions. Pupils are encouraged to listen, talk, and reflect on the topics explored and to show respect for views that may differ from their own. It is intended that pupils should begin to recognise their place and influence in the world around them and to show this positively. The curriculum seeks to promote the school values of respect and equality through topics taught, as well as day to day social interactions with their peers.
Religious Education (RE)
At NRHS, the Key Stage 1 RE curriculum intends to expose pupils to a variety of religions and beliefs while describing their own perspectives on faith, including those who do not follow a religion. Respect and understanding are embedded in the curriculum and ethos while promoting the spiritual, moral, social, cultural and intellectual development of our pupils. This in turn supports pupils to become tolerant and inclusive members of society. The RE curriculum intends for pupils to appreciate and value how different faiths are represented in the lives and practices of its followers and how this is applied in real life. Parents have the statutory right to withdraw their child from all or part of the RE curriculum.

Subject intent
The information below highlights the intent behind each subject in Years 3 & 4, including the knowledge and skills we aspire for pupils to achieve.
English
At NRHS, the Key Stage 2 English curriculum intends for pupils to develop their love of reading, writing and discussion. We intend to support pupils to develop confidence and the grammatical skills needed to read and write cohesively. By creating an engaging environment based on a variety of texts, we encourage pupils’ natural curiosity, inspiring them to become lifelong learners with a positive attitude towards reading and writing. Through developing their English skills pupils will go on to be confident when sharing and expressing themselves through verbal and written methods.
Maths
At NRHS, the Key Stage 2 Maths curriculum intends to embed key mathematical skills so that pupils can become fluent in the fundamentals of mathematics, reason mathematically, and problem solve by applying their skills and knowledge. We intend to build on pupils’ confidence enabling them to apply their mathematical understanding with more standardised approaches and become fluent in the application of mathematical concepts. This in turn supports them to recognise the real-life situations where mathematical competence is a necessary and important, real-life skill.
Science
At NRHS, the Key Stage 2 Science curriculum continues to encourage pupils to be inquisitive and to develop their curiosity about the universe. Learning extends and enhances their scientific enquiry skills: classifying, comparing and contrasting, predicting, making models, gathering data, measuring, observing. Our skills-based focus intends to develop the scientific skills required to understand the uses and implications of science, today and for the future.
Art
At NRHS, the Key Stage 2 Art curriculum intends to give pupils opportunities to express their thoughts, feelings and ideas and demonstrate their creativity using a variety of materials building on skills previously taught. Pupils will be able to express their views, preferences and observations of different genres with confidence. Pupils will continue to develop their critical thinking and evaluation skills justifying their opinions. Moreover, it enables pupils to develop a natural sense of wonder and curiosity about the world around them whilst engaging and inspiring them.
Computing
At NRHS, the Key Stage 2 Computing curriculum intends for pupils to explore, analyse and present information in different ways, this enables pupils to think about how information is used, stored and interpreted. This allows pupils to be computer literate and to use computing skills to develop the confidence to be creative thinkers and learners in a variety of real-life contexts. The curriculum aims to build computing experiences which prepares pupils to live safely in a digital society and to be flexible and resilient to cope with technology that is always changing and advancing.
Design and Technology (DT)
At NRHS, the Key Stage 2 DT curriculum intends is to explore pupils’ creativity and inventiveness so they can express their unique ideas as individuals. The DT curriculum includes Graphic Design, Textiles and Cooking lessons which intend to provide pupils the opportunity to become innovative, enterprising and resourceful. The aim of the curriculum is that pupils will be inspired by Engineers, Designers, Chefs and Architects to enable them to create a range of structures, mechanisms, electrical systems and food products with a real-life purpose. This gives the pupils inspiration for future careers in this field.
Geography
The Key Stage 2 Geography curriculum intends to inform pupils about the enormity of our world. The curriculum encourages pupils to use maps and atlases so that pupils can develop an understanding of different countries, continents, seas and oceans. Through studying the natural and human environments, as well as physical and human processes, the curriculum aims to provide pupils with a sense of awe and wonder about the world they live in, building a sense of curiosity and asking questions so that they are keen to continue learning about the world in Key Stage 3.
History
At NRHS, the Key Stage 2 History curriculum intends to create in the pupils a sense of interest and enjoyment in this subject, while further developing their understanding of important historical events and people, and developing skills such as critical thinking, analysing evidence and discussing opposing points of view. The curriculum intends to provide pupils with opportunities to extend their abilities to nurture their opinions and make judgements concerning things which happened in the past, and to enjoy the rich trove of stories which make up our history.
Horticulture
At NRHS, the Key Stage 2 Horticulture curriculum intends for pupils to continue on their adventure into the natural world. It is intended that pupils will build on their basic skills and knowledge in the production of food crops. The curriculum provides pupils with the opportunity to demonstrate their confidence, patience, perseverance, resilience and mental wellbeing in a safe outdoor space. The curriculum will enable pupils to explore the relationships between living things and the environment, whilst promoting independent thinking and learning.
PE
At NRHS, the PE curriculum intends to adhere to the philosophy of ‘Sport for All’. The school aims to deliver an exciting and enjoyable experience for all pupils acquiring the skills and knowledge in line with the National Curriculum. The broad and balanced curriculum aims to re-cap, re-call and build on prior knowledge using a range of physical activities. Through a carefully structured programme, we aim for pupils to build their physical, social and mental skills, enabling them to fully participate in a range of roles in PE. All pupils at NRHS have the opportunity to participate in an extensive Extra Curricular/Enrichment programme, which develops pupils’ confidence in applying their skills in competitive situations.
PSHE
At NRHS, the Key Stage 2 PSHE Curriculum intends to promote self-awareness of pupils’ personal development and social interactions. Pupils are encouraged to listen, talk, and reflect on the topics explored and to understand and respect a range of different views and opinions. It is intended that pupils begin to recognise their place and influence in the world around them and how to use this positively, whilst developing skills and attributes such as resilience, confidence, teamwork, risk management and critical thinking.
Religious Education (RE)
At NRHS, the Key Stage 2 RE curriculum intends to provide pupils with opportunities to explore a variety of religions that are reflective of our local community, while building on prior knowledge and skills. Pupils are encouraged to reflect of their own religious beliefs and those of others, including those who do not follow a religion. Respect and understanding are embedded in the curriculum and ethos while promoting the spiritual, moral, social, cultural and intellectual development of our pupils. This in turn supports pupils to become tolerant and inclusive members of society. Parents have the statutory right to withdraw their child from all or part of the RE curriculum.
Spanish
At NRHS, the Key Stage 2 Spanish curriculum intends to ignite a love for language learning. Our pupils are exposed to a foreign language, focusing on building a strong foundation in Spanish vocabulary and basic grammar, fostering effective communication skills. Our intentions are to instil an appreciation for diverse cultures, for pupils to broaden their horizons and develop their confidence so that they are better able to communicate in preparation for life in multi-cultural Britain.
